originality.rationale: Direct comparison with accessible primary full texts shows no stated sharp phase-independent first-two-odd-Hermite polynomial or optimized quartic-to-sextic three-mode normal form for (8,4,1). The general 2017 Hermite identity supplies a route to deducing the formulas and is explicitly credited, so the risk of seeing them as an implicit special case remains. residual_risks: The general 2017 Hermite norm identity may be considered implicit broader coverage after explicit substitution; originality of a finite computed special case is sensitive to this interpretation.

value.rationale: The unresolved parity-constrained (8,4,1) sharp problem naturally suggests its first odd spectral modes. An exact global two-mode deficit with a sharp fourth-order stability constant, together with a unique cancellation by the third mode and a positive sextic remainder, describes a symmetry-enforced degeneracy and the cost of finite-dimensional spectral truncation. This is a precise reusable finite-band benchmark rather than a claimed unrestricted sharp inequality.
